threats.name: Agent principal impersonation
threats.description: A different principal presents itself as the authorized stable agent principal.

threats.name: Controller or mandator substitution
threats.description: An agent or adapter replaces the legitimate controlling/mandating principal with another principal.

threats.name: Runtime instance substitution
threats.description: A different runtime/workload instance attempts to inherit runtime-sensitive authority from the stable agent identity.

threats.name: Model substitution
threats.description: A materially different model is substituted where policy binds authority to model/runtime provenance.

threats.name: Credential or key theft
threats.description: Stolen authentication/signing material is replayed to impersonate an otherwise legitimate agent or controller.

threats.name: Identity or key rotation race
threats.description: Old and new identity/key generations are raced so stale material is accepted as current.

threats.name: Mission-to-intent semantic overreach
threats.description: A broad natural-language mission is translated into a typed intent with authority-significant permissions the principal did not approve.

threats.name: Prompt-injection intent confusion
threats.description: Untrusted instructions cause the model to reinterpret the principal's mission or propose unauthorized intent.

threats.name: Approved-intent substitution
threats.description: A different typed intent is substituted after principal approval or qualification.

threats.name: Deceptive or spoofed approval
threats.adversary: phisher, malicious UI, or compromised agent
threats.description: The system claims principal approval that did not occur or misrepresents the exact intent/action being approved.

threats.name: Consent UI semantic mismatch
threats.description: The user-visible approval summary differs materially from the typed intent or exact action that receives authority.

threats.name: Confused deputy
threats.description: A less-authorized party induces a more-authorized agent or broker to exercise authority for the wrong principal, resource, or purpose.

threats.name: Capability scope expansion
threats.description: A child or translated authorization adds capabilities, resources, audiences, validity, or roles absent from the qualified parent.

threats.name: Consumable-budget fan-out duplication
threats.description: Multiple children each receive individually valid-looking allocations whose sum exceeds the parent's conserved budget.

threats.name: Unauthorized re-delegation
threats.description: A delegate passes authority onward without explicit qualified permission to re-delegate.

threats.name: Delegation cycle or depth exhaustion
threats.description: Cyclic or excessively deep delegation consumes verifier resources or obscures the actual authority source.

threats.name: Stale authority replay
threats.description: A previously valid positive grant/delegation/currentness result is replayed after it is no longer current.

threats.name: Revoked authority continued use
threats.description: An agent continues consequential execution after a relevant authority generation becomes revoked or superseded.

threats.name: Audience or provider substitution
threats.description: Authority intended for one audience/provider is exercised against another.

threats.name: Policy or rulebook substitution
threats.description: A weaker policy/profile is swapped in while retaining superficially similar authority identifiers.

threats.name: Currentness TOCTOU race
threats.description: Authority is qualified as current and then revoked or materially changed before effect dispatch.

threats.name: Runtime-attestation downgrade
threats.description: Weaker or self-asserted runtime provenance is substituted for a policy-required assurance level.

threats.name: Compromised runtime or model
threats.adversary: malware, malicious model, or compromised host
threats.description: The active agent runtime behaves adversarially while possessing otherwise valid identity or authority inputs.

threats.name: Software supply-chain compromise
threats.description: Agent/broker/verifier software is replaced or modified before execution.

threats.name: Authority broker compromise
threats.description: The credential-less authority broker leaks secrets, forges qualification, or dispatches effects outside qualified scope.

threats.name: Tool-argument escape
threats.adversary: malicious model, prompt injection, or tool server
threats.description: An action remains in an allowed tool class but authority-significant arguments escape the QualifiedIntent or authority envelope.

threats.name: Canonical-action ambiguity
threats.description: Different authority-relevant actions collide or are treated as equivalent because canonicalization/profile identity is ambiguous.

threats.name: Model self-certification bypass
threats.description: Model output asserting compliance is accepted in place of deterministic constraint qualification.

threats.name: Cross-action replay
threats.description: A valid authorization/receipt for one exact action is replayed against a changed action, resource, amount, or recipient.

threats.name: Long-lived secret exfiltration
threats.adversary: prompt injector, malicious tool, or compromised model
threats.description: Reusable credentials exposed to model context are extracted and reused outside the intended action.

threats.name: Capability-handle replay
threats.adversary: agent or attacker possessing an opaque handle
threats.description: An opaque capability reference is reused after current authority, audience, scope, or use limits changed.

threats.name: Protocol translation authority widening
threats.description: Translation into A2A/MCP/OAuth/AP2 or another protocol silently broadens scope, validity, audience, or delegation.

threats.name: Malicious A2A peer or Agent Card
threats.description: Discovery/task metadata misrepresents capabilities, identity, endpoints, or trust-relevant facts to induce unsafe delegation/action.

threats.name: Malicious MCP server or tool metadata
threats.description: Tool descriptions, schemas, resources, or responses are crafted to induce credential leakage or unauthorized actions.

threats.name: External authorization semantic mismatch
threats.description: A downstream token/credential encodes materially different scope semantics from the qualified Mycelix authority.

threats.name: Commerce mandate mismatch
threats.adversary: merchant, shopping agent, or payment adapter
threats.description: Commerce/payment mandate semantics diverge from the QualifiedIntent, conserved budget, or exact purchase action.

threats.name: Duplicate effect by retry
threats.adversary: agent, network fault, or malicious provider
threats.description: A caller retries after an uncertain result and causes the same consequential intent to produce multiple external effects.

threats.name: Ambiguous commit exploitation
threats.description: A provider returns an error/timeout while the effect may have committed, inducing unsafe retry or inconsistent local state.

threats.name: Partial multi-effect completion
threats.description: A multi-step action partially commits and local logic incorrectly treats the whole transaction as committed or not committed.

threats.name: External provider equivocation
threats.description: A provider presents inconsistent receipts/status to different observers for the same effect attempt.

threats.name: Receipt replay or substitution
threats.description: A valid receipt is reused for a different action/attempt or substituted into another evidence package.

threats.name: Receipt equivocation or tampering
threats.description: Different receipt facts are presented under the same apparent receipt identity, or receipt content is altered without detection.

threats.name: Evidence withholding or incomplete view
threats.adversary: malicious agent, node, provider, or verifier
threats.description: Security-relevant evidence is omitted so a partial observation appears sufficient for positive qualification.

threats.name: Malicious independent verifier
threats.description: A verifier falsely reports a package as valid, suppresses a failure, or uses a weaker verification profile.

threats.name: Over-disclosure and cross-context correlation
threats.description: An agent discloses more identity, credential, intent, or evidence than necessary, enabling privacy loss or cross-context linkage.

threats.name: Colluding sub-agents
threats.description: Multiple agents coordinate to exploit delegation, budgets, evidence views, or provider boundaries while each appears individually compliant.

threats.name: Network partition or delayed revocation
threats.description: Partition/delay prevents timely observation of revocation/currentness or produces divergent evidence views.

threats.name: Resource exhaustion
threats.adversary: malicious peer, agent, or evidence producer
threats.description: Unbounded delegation, intent, action, receipt, proof, or evidence inputs exhaust verifier/broker resources.

threats.name: Malicious or ambiguous Mycelix network view
threats.adversary: malicious nodes or partitioned DHT authorities
threats.description: Network data is incomplete, conflicting, reordered, or adversarially presented and is mistaken for authoritative global current state.

threats.name: Valid authority but substantively bad outcome
threats.description: An action is correctly authorized yet factually wrong, unsafe, unwise, unfair, or harmful; authority verification is misrepresented as outcome correctness.
